subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: What durable trust model should OpenClaw use for elevated cron jobs and heartbeat turns?
rationale: The issue changes the security boundary for elevated exec, persisted cron definitions, and heartbeat provenance, so automation should not choose the permanent API or migration behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Unify With Scheduling Provenance
options.body: Use #71712's Gateway-owned provenance model as the authority and add elevated approval as a decision receipt tied to a schedule or heartbeat definition.

options.title: Add Narrow Per-Job Elevated Approval
options.body: Introduce a smaller cron `elevated` flag that only elevated senders can set, while separately tracking heartbeat approval metadata.

options.title: Remove Internal Elevated Wildcards
options.body: Fail closed for `cron-event` and `heartbeat` elevated access until operators recreate trusted jobs through an approved path.

recommendation.title: Unify With Scheduling Provenance
recommendation.body: Use #71712's Gateway-owned provenance model as the authority and add elevated approval as a decision receipt tied to a schedule or heartbeat definition.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the closest recent cron caller-scope/provenance mitigation and is best positioned to connect this request with the broader scheduling RFC.
